name: WALGREEN CO
same_company_evidence: Payee Deerfield, IL is Walgreen Co's corporate home. The Ohio project behind the $750,000 Economic Development Grant is the Perrysburg Township distribution center in Wood County, 350 new and 679 retained jobs (JobsOhio commitment reported July 2018; Toledo Blade, May 21, 2018).
ohio_outcome: Nothing found showing the Perrysburg Township (Wood County) distribution center closed or was cut. The two flagged items are elsewhere: a May 2023 cut of about 10 percent of the Deerfield, Illinois corporate staff, and a 2026 store closing in St. Louis County, Missouri.
source: Google News RSS 'Walgreens Ohio distribution center close layoffs' and 'Walgreens Wood County Ohio jobs distribution'; Toledo Blade 2018-05-21; data/commitments.csv
notes: Walgreens went private in 2025 and has closed stores across the country, so single-store closings keep surfacing. None of them is the Ohio facility the grant paid for.

name: FORWARD AIR INC
same_company_evidence: Same company. Forward Air's Ohio project is the national less-than-truckload hub at Rickenbacker in Columbus, Franklin County: a $750,000 Revitalization Grant, 50 new and 403 retained jobs (commitment reported March 2021), alongside a $40 million hub expansion announced July 2020.
ohio_outcome: No report of the Columbus hub closing or shrinking. The expansion announced in July 2020 went ahead, and Forward Air was still named as the operator of that network in June 2026 trade coverage. The flagged layoffs are company-wide cost cuts, the 2023 round and the 2024 round that followed the Omni Logistics acquisition.
source: Google News RSS 'Forward Air Columbus Ohio layoffs', 'Forward Air Rickenbacker Columbus hub'; Transport Topics and Columbus Dispatch 2020-07-27; FreightWaves 2026-06-11; data/commitments.csv
notes: Worth a second look if an Ohio WARN notice for Forward Air ever turns up; none was found in news coverage.

name: WILLIAMS LEA INC
same_company_evidence: Payee is Columbus, Ohio. The grant is a $700,000 Workforce Grant against 550 new jobs in Franklin County (commitment reported December 2019), paid out in the 2020 and 2022 filings.
ohio_outcome: The flagged story is about Williams Lea's India staff after RRD bought the company; it says nothing about Ohio. No report was found of the Columbus operation closing or cutting jobs.
source: Google News RSS 'Williams Lea Columbus Ohio jobs', 'Williams Lea acquisition RRD 2025 jobs'; The Federal 2025-01-22; Outsource Accelerator 2025-01-04; data/commitments.csv
notes: The company was sold after both grant years: RRD completed its acquisition of Williams Lea in January 2025. What happened to the Columbus headcount after the sale is not reported anywhere I could find, so the 550-job commitment is unverified rather than disproved.

name: GENERAL DYNAMICS LAND SYSTEMS INC
same_company_evidence: Same company, wrong plant. Both flagged headlines come from the London Free Press and concern General Dynamics Land Systems Canada in London, Ontario.
ohio_outcome: The Ohio operation is the Joint Systems Manufacturing Center in Lima, Allen County. No closure or job cut there was found; the 2026 headline is about growth, not layoffs, at the Ontario supplier.
source: Google News RSS 'Lima Ohio tank plant General Dynamics jobs layoffs'; London Free Press 2025-03-24 and 2026-07-20; data/grants_raw.csv
notes: One of the two flagged headlines explicitly says the deal means growth, not layoffs.

name: BOOZ ALLEN HAMILTON INC
same_company_evidence: Same company. The Ohio project is the Dayton-area digital hub in Beavercreek, Greene County: a $500,000 Economic Development Grant plus a $150,000 Workforce Grant, 60 new and 290 retained jobs (commitment reported July 2019). Two of the three grant filings name Beavercreek, OH as the payee address.
ohio_outcome: No report of the Beavercreek hub closing or being cut. The flagged layoffs were announced from McLean, Virginia and described as company-wide, tied to federal consulting cutbacks.
source: Google News RSS 'Booz Allen Hamilton Beavercreek Ohio jobs'; Virginia Business 2025-10-27; Investopedia 2025-05-23; Consulting.us 2019-04-03; data/commitments.csv, data/grants_raw.csv
notes: Booz Allen's company-wide cuts in 2025 were large, so an Ohio share is plausible, but no source puts any of them in Ohio.

name: CITY OF TOLEDO
same_company_evidence: The payee is the City of Toledo, a municipal government.
ohio_outcome: Nothing happened to the grantee. The flagged headline is the city shutting down illegal after-hours clubs in 2021, which is the city acting as a regulator, not the city failing.
source: Google News RSS; WNWO 2021-07-20
notes: The word 'shutting down' in the headline is what tripped the scan.

name: DOLLAR TREE DISTRIBUTION INC
same_company_evidence: Same company, wrong state. The flagged closure is the Dollar Tree distribution center in Marietta, Oklahoma, wrecked by an EF-4 tornado in April 2024; the coverage is all Oklahoma outlets (KOCO, KOSU, KFOR). The Ohio project is the distribution center in Morrow County, 400 jobs, a $400,000 Workforce Grant (commitment reported February 2019).
ohio_outcome: No report of the Morrow County distribution center closing or shrinking. Marietta, Oklahoma itself was rebuilt: Dollar Tree broke ground on a $50 million replacement in September 2025 with 400 jobs.
source: Google News RSS 'Dollar Tree Marietta Ohio distribution center', 'Morrow County Dollar Tree distribution center close'; KOSU 2024-05-30; Marietta Times 2025-09-30; Morrow County Sentinel 2018-05-20; data/commitments.csv
notes: Marietta, Ohio and Marietta, Oklahoma are the trap here. The damaged center is the Oklahoma one.

name: SIERRA NEVADA CORPORATION
same_company_evidence: Both flagged headlines are about Sierra Nevada Memorial Hospital in Grass Valley, California, which is run by CommonSpirit Health. The grantee is Sierra Nevada Corporation of Sparks, Nevada, an aerospace and defense contractor. Different industry, different state, different owner.
ohio_outcome: Sierra Nevada's Ohio operation is in the Dayton area, Montgomery County, and has been growing: a JobsOhio Economic Development Grant reported in December 2024 counted 200 new jobs on top of 147 retained, and a $2.5 million site grant followed in March 2025.
source: Google News RSS 'Sierra Nevada Dayton Ohio jobs layoffs'; National Nurses United 2026-08-05; data/commitments.csv
notes: Name collision only.

name: FirstMerit Corporation
entity_filed: FirstMerit Corporation itself, as the acquired company
same_company_evidence: Same company. The payee is FirstMerit Corporation of Akron, Ohio, and the stories are about Akron-based FirstMerit Bank being bought by Huntington Bancshares of Columbus.
ohio_outcome: FirstMerit stopped existing as an Akron company. Huntington announced the purchase on January 26, 2016 and closed it on August 16, 2016. In March 2016 the two banks said they would close more than 100 branches, nearly 50 of them in Northeast Ohio, and layoffs were expected. Huntington did keep the Akron headquarters building operation and said in November 2018 that it would add jobs there; it put the historic Akron skyscraper it got in the deal up for sale in March 2019. No jobs figure for the Ohio branch closings was reported.
source: Google News RSS 'FirstMerit Huntington Akron headquarters jobs branches close 2016'; WKYC 2016-01-26; Cleveland 19 News 2016-01-26; Cleveland.com 2016-03-10; Akron Beacon Journal 2018-11-27; Columbus Dispatch 2019-03-21; data/grants_raw.csv
notes: This is a sale, not an insolvency, so read 'Confirmed failure' here as 'the Ohio operation was sold off', which is what the flag was asking. Timing caveat: the $500,000 grant and the announcement of the sale both fall in 2016, and I could not establish which came first, so this could also be read as 'Before the grant'. FirstMerit does not appear in the JobsOhio commitment reports, so the purpose of the grant is unknown.

name: HOWMET AEROSPACE INC
same_company_evidence: Same company, wrong plants. The two flagged headlines are the LaPorte, Indiana plant (WNDU) and the Wichita Falls, Texas plant (News Channel 6).
ohio_outcome: No Ohio closure or cut was confirmed. Howmet's Ohio grant sites are Cuyahoga Heights in Cuyahoga County (1,000 jobs retained, commitment reported September 2021), a Stark County project with RMI Titanium (40 new, 115 retained, January 2022) and a Ross County project (4 new, 26 retained, November 2022). None of them shows up in closure coverage.
source: Google News RSS 'Howmet Aerospace Ohio layoffs plant', 'Howmet Aerospace Barberton wheels Ohio', 'Howmet Cuyahoga Heights Arconic Cleveland layoffs'; WNDU 2020-09-15; data/commitments.csv
notes: One loose end. An Akron Beacon Journal headline dated June 12, 2020, 'Barberton firm cuts workforce by more than half with latest layoffs', comes back repeatedly on Howmet-plus-Ohio searches, and Howmet does run a forged wheel plant in Barberton. The Beacon Journal blocks direct fetches and the page is not in the Wayback Machine, so I could not read it or confirm the company. If that story is about Howmet, Ohio saw a deep 2020 cut between the 2019 and 2022 grants. Treat as unverified. SETTLED (Nov 3, 2026): the Barberton headline is not a funded site. JobsOhio's own monthly reports put all three Howmet/Arconic awards in Cuyahoga (Sept 2021, 1,000 retained), Stark (Jan 2022, with RMI Titanium) and Ross (Nov 2022, and Arconic June 2018) counties. Barberton is in Summit County and appears in no JobsOhio record, so the June 2020 cut there is not a cut at a funded site. Verdict stands.

name: 80 ACRES URBAN AGRICULTURE INC
entity_filed: 80 Acres Urban Agriculture, Inc., the grant payee itself
court: Not seen; reported as a Chapter 7 filing
same_company_evidence: Same company. The payee is 80 Acres Urban Agriculture, Inc. of Hamilton, Ohio, and the coverage is Hamilton and Cincinnati outlets reporting on the Hamilton vertical farming company. The JobsOhio commitment reported in May 2020 is a $500,000 Economic Development Grant in Butler and Hamilton counties for 125 new and 29 retained jobs.
ohio_outcome: The Hamilton, Ohio farm and headquarters closed. The company announced on August 3, 2026 that it was winding down, and the Journal-News reported on August 5, 2026 that a collapsed acquisition deal triggered the shutdown and eliminated 145 Hamilton jobs. Sites in Florence, Kentucky (about 120 jobs) and San Antonio, Texas (166 jobs) closed at the same time. The company filed Chapter 7 on August 26, 2026 with more than $100 million in debt. Terminated employees sued in August 2026, and the chief executive said in October 2026 that 'we ran out of time'.
source: Google News RSS '80 Acres Farms Hamilton Ohio', '80 Acres Farms bankruptcy chapter 11 Delaware filing'; Journal-News 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-05; FOX19 2026-08-03; Law360 2026-08-26; Cincinnati Enquirer 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-27; WKRC 2026-10-11; data/commitments.csv
notes: The clearest case in this batch: grant in 2020, Ohio site closed and the payee liquidated in 2026. The docket number was not retrieved; Law360 reported the Chapter 7 and the debt figure.

name: REPUBLIC STEEL INC
entity_filed: Republic Steel, the grant payee; no bankruptcy filing found, the mills were idled
same_company_evidence: Same company. The payee is Republic Steel of Lorain, Ohio, and the coverage is Cleveland, Canton and Lorain outlets reporting on Republic Steel's Ohio mills. The JobsOhio commitment reported in February 2019 is a $500,000 Workforce Grant in Lorain County for 125 new jobs.
ohio_outcome: Both Ohio mills went dark. Republic Steel idled steelmaking at its Canton mill indefinitely on August 10, 2023, furloughing what local coverage described as hundreds of workers, and idled Lackawanna, New York the same day. The Lorain mill, the site of the grant, had been idle since earlier and was still idle in November 2025, when Recycling Today reported it might draw international investment. In February 2024 the company agreed to a $700,000 federal penalty over chemical releases from the shuttered Canton and Lorain plants, and inspectors found leaking chemicals and mold at the empty Lorain site in May 2024. By November 2025 Lorain officials were courting new steelmakers for up to 1,200 jobs at the site.
source: Google News RSS 'Republic Steel Lorain Ohio', 'Republic Steel Canton closing jobs', 'Republic Steel Lorain mill idled'; Cleveland 19 News 2023-08-10; FOX 8 2023-08-10; Ideastream 2023-08-11; Canton Repository 2023-08-10 and 2023-08-16; WKYC 2024-02-05; Recycling Today 2025-11-21
notes: Exact headcount not settled. Local coverage says 'hundreds' at Canton and I could not retrieve a WARN figure; Ideastream, FOX 8 and the Canton Repository all blocked direct fetches. Canton Repository also reported in August 2023 that Republic owed millions in back taxes and to unpaid vendors.

name: CITY OF CLEVELAND
same_company_evidence: The payee is the City of Cleveland, a municipal government that took a series of small Revitalization Grants in 2019.
ohio_outcome: Nothing happened to the grantee. The flagged headline is the city defending its decision to close a bar and grill after a shooting, which is the city acting as a regulator.
source: Google News RSS; WKYC 2025-09-10; data/commitments.csv
notes: The word 'close' in the headline is what tripped the scan.

name: Dmax Ltd
same_company_evidence: Same company. The payee is Dmax, Ltd. of Moraine, Ohio, the GM and Isuzu diesel engine joint venture, and the story is about that plant.
ohio_outcome: The Moraine plant stopped production only briefly, after a fatal shooting on May 19, 2023, and then resumed. DMAX is still running and still growing: a $7,000,000 JobsOhio Economic Development Grant reported in August 2024 counted 814 retained jobs, and in April 2026 the Dayton Daily News covered a DMAX expansion in Brookville, calling it 'a significant plant in the GM world'.
source: Google News RSS 'DMAX Moraine Ohio plant jobs'; WDTN 2023-05-19; Dayton Daily News 2026-04-14; data/commitments.csv
notes: A production stop after a shooting is not a closure. The scan's 'shuts down production' phrasing caused the flag.

name: TEKNI-PLEX INC
same_company_evidence: Same company, wrong plant. The January 2026 closure is Tekni-Plex's Milwaukee plant at the former Amcor site, per Plastics News.
ohio_outcome: The Ohio operation grew. Tekni-Plex's Ohio project is the specialty molded fiber plant in Van Wert, announced in 2023 with a $400,000 JobsOhio grant for 100 jobs, and it got a second $400,000 grant reported in September 2025 for 40 more jobs on top of those 100. No Ohio closure or cut found. An earlier, much smaller Ohio grant in Lucas County dates from 2015.
source: Google News RSS 'Tekni-Plex Ohio plant'; Plastics News 2026-01-26; Food Industry Executive 2024-10-03; data/commitments.csv
notes: The flagged Yahoo Finance headline lumps three companies' January layoffs together, which is why it surfaced.

name: AER LINGUS LIMITED
same_company_evidence: Same company. The $400,000 grant, paid in fiscal 2024, bought air service: the Cleveland to Dublin route, which Aer Lingus launched in May 2023 with city and state incentives.
ohio_outcome: The Ohio service survived. This project's own route data in the repository shows Cleveland to Dublin flying from May 2023 through June 2026, 38 months, 239 flights in 2025 and about 91,000 passengers, marked 'still flying (June 2026)'. Aer Lingus did trim the Cleveland schedule for 2026 to weekend-focused flying (Cleveland.com, October 2, 2025), and it dropped several US routes in 2026 including Minneapolis and Denver, but Cleveland was not among them. The flagged job cuts, 500 posts and manager layoffs, are in Ireland.
source: data/air_service_routes.csv (Aer Lingus CLE-DUB); Google News RSS 'Aer Lingus Cleveland Dublin route cut 2026'; Cleveland.com 2025-10-02; Simple Flying 2026-07-16; The Business Journals 2026-07-17; BBC 2026-07-16
notes: Worth watching: the schedule was cut back to weekends for 2026 and Aer Lingus listed Cleveland among its emptier US routes in February 2026. That is a reduction in the thing the grant bought, not a closure.

name: CUSTOM GLASS SOLUTIONS LLC
same_company_evidence: Same company, wrong plant. The flagged closure is the Trumbauersville plant in Bucks County, Pennsylvania, 105 jobs, announced February 27, 2025.
ohio_outcome: The Ohio operations grew rather than shrank. Custom Glass Solutions named Upper Sandusky its new corporate headquarters in May 2025 and celebrated an expansion of its Seneca County plant in June 2025. Its Ohio grant sites are Fostoria in Seneca County (a $275,000 grant for 80 jobs reported May 2019, then $150,000 for 148 new and 419 retained in July 2021) and Millbury in Ottawa County (2016). No Ohio closure found.
source: Google News RSS 'Custom Glass Solutions Ohio', 'Custom Glass Solutions Fostoria Millbury layoffs'; DELCO.Today 2025-03-04; WFMZ 2025-02-27; Business Wire 2025-05-09; wtol.com 2025-06-09; whatnow.com 2026-03-12; data/commitments.csv
notes: One near-miss worth recording: a March 12, 2026 story headlined 'Northwest Ohio Manufacturing Facility to Close, 64 Employees Face Layoffs' sits close to this company in search results, but reading it shows the company is The Boelter Companies, operating as Custom Deco LLC, at 1343 Miami St. in Toledo, closing May 29, 2026. Custom Deco, not Custom Glass.

name: CONSTRUCTCONNECT INC
same_company_evidence: Not a story about the company at all. The flagged item is a Stelco article published on constructconnect.com, which is ConstructConnect's own construction news site. The company is the author, not the subject.
ohio_outcome: No report of the Cincinnati operation closing or cutting jobs. ConstructConnect does not appear in the JobsOhio commitment reports under that name, so the Ohio project behind the grant is not identified.
source: Google News RSS 'ConstructConnect Cincinnati layoffs sold' and 'ConstructConnect Cincinnati jobs office' (no closure coverage); data/reversals.csv
notes: Separate finding, not a failure: the 2022 filing records a negative grant amount for ConstructConnect in Cincinnati, minus $125,000 (data/reversals.csv), meaning money came back or a commitment was reversed. That belongs in the clawback thread, not this one.

name: iMFLUX Inc
entity_filed: Procter & Gamble closed its subsidiary; no bankruptcy
same_company_evidence: Same company. The payee is iMFLUX Inc of West Chester, Ohio, a Procter & Gamble injection molding subsidiary, and the stories name iMFLUX and its Hamilton, Ohio site. The grant is $350,000 in the 2015 filing.
ohio_outcome: The Ohio site closed. Plastics News reported on April 7, 2023 that iMFLUX was closing its Ohio site and switching to royalty-free licensing, and the Cincinnati Enquirer and WCPO reported on May 1 and 2, 2023 that P&G was shutting the Hamilton subsidiary and laying off 122 workers. In December 2024 WKRC reported that a Cincinnati firm had bought the former P&G manufacturing site.
source: Google News RSS 'iMFLUX Hamilton Ohio'; Plastics News 2023-04-07 and 2023-04-13; WCPO 2023-05-01; Cincinnati Enquirer 2023-05-02; WKRC 2024-12-21; data/grants_raw.csv
notes: Grant in 2015, Ohio site closed in 2023 with 122 jobs lost. Clean case. No court record because this was a parent shutting a subsidiary, not an insolvency.

name: Mercy Health
same_company_evidence: Mixed. The 2024 story is Bon Secours Mercy Health, the same Cincinnati-based system as the payee. The 2019 story is a different Mercy: the Springfield News-Leader was covering Mercy of Springfield, Missouri, an unrelated health system.
ohio_outcome: No Ohio closure. The February 2024 cuts hit close to 300 remote workers across the system as scheduling moved online (WFMJ, February 16, 2024, which noted some of them were in the Mahoning Valley). The grant-funded Ohio project is in Hamilton County, a $300,000 Economic Development Grant reported in September 2015 for 175 new and 1,050 retained jobs, and that Cincinnati operation is not reported closing. No jobs figure specific to Ohio was published.
source: Google News RSS 'Mercy Health Cincinnati hospital closing layoffs'; WLWT 2024-02-22; WFMJ 2024-02-16; Springfield News-Leader 2019-06-20; data/commitments.csv
notes: The 2019 headline is a name collision with Mercy in Missouri. The 2024 cuts were remote scheduling staff, system-wide, and cannot be pinned to the grant site.

name: CHARLES RIVER LABORATORIES INC
same_company_evidence: Same company, wrong sites. The flagged layoffs are company-wide and at the Wilmington, Massachusetts headquarters, per NBC Boston in February 2026 and the Boston Business Journal in November 2025.
ohio_outcome: No Ohio closure or cut found. Charles River's Ohio footprint grew around the grant years: the Ashland site added 140 jobs in 2019, took a $300,000 grant reported in February 2020 for 140 new and 929 retained jobs, and in May 2022 announced a $212 million, 200,000 square foot expansion with 500 more jobs. A second $300,000 grant reported in April 2022 covers an Allen County project, 105 new and 224 retained jobs.
source: Google News RSS 'Charles River Ohio site expansion jobs', 'Charles River Spencerville Ashland Ohio layoffs'; Ashland Times-Gazette 2022-05-25; Richland Source 2022-05-25; The Business Journals 2025-11-14; NBC Boston 2026-02-05; data/commitments.csv
notes: Charles River has been shrinking overall, so the Ashland 500-job promise is worth checking against payroll data, but no Ohio layoff or closure is reported.

name: CONAGRA BRANDS
same_company_evidence: Same company, wrong plant. The flagged closure is the Birds Eye plant in Beaver Dam, Wisconsin, 252 jobs, reported April 9 and 10, 2024.
ohio_outcome: No Ohio closure found, and both Ohio plants had been expanding. The Troy plant in Miami County, which makes Slim Jims, took a $300,000 JobsOhio grant reported in February 2022 for 100 new jobs on 929 retained, after a $70 million expansion finished around 2020. The Archbold plant in Fulton County added 100 jobs in January 2020.
source: Google News RSS 'Conagra Ohio plant closing Archbold Troy', 'Conagra Troy Ohio plant jobs Slim Jim'; Food Dive 2024-04-10; Milwaukee Journal Sentinel 2024-04-09; WTOL 2020-01-27; Food Manufacturing 2022-01-12; data/commitments.csv
notes: The payee address on the 2023 filing is El Paso, Texas, but the Ohio grants under the Conagra Foods Packaged Foods entity point at Troy and Archbold.
